literal: Chounu made Baoyin Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: Chounu made Baoyin grand tutor.

literal: Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue and others to defeat Chounu at Anding, pursued and captured Chounu and Baoyin, and sent them both to the capital.
idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue to defeat Chounu at Anding, captured Chounu and Baoyin, and sent them to the capital.

literal: An edict placed them in the central avenue outside Changhe Gate; capital gentlemen and ladies gathered to watch—for three days in all.
idiomatic: They were displayed in the avenue outside Changhe Gate while the capital watched for three days.

literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenjun and Yellow Gate Vice Director Gao Daomu were both old friends of Baoyin; the two sided with him and spoke to Emperor Zhuang, saying his rebellious traces belonged to the former dynasty and they hoped to save him.
idiomatic: Li Shenjun and Gao Daomu, Baoyin's old friends, told Emperor Zhuang his treason was under the former reign and hoped to save him.

literal: It happened that Responding-Edict Wang Daoxi had just come from outside; Emperor Zhuang asked what Daoxi had heard outside.
idiomatic: Responding-Edict Wang Daoxi arrived; the emperor asked what he had heard outside.

literal: Daoxi said: "I only heard that Your Majesty does not wish to kill Xiao Baoyin.
idiomatic: Daoxi said, "I only heard that Your Majesty will not kill Xiao Baoyin.

literal: People say Director Li and Yellow Gate Gao are intimate with Baoyin and both stand where speech carries weight—they can surely preserve him.
idiomatic: People say Director Li and Yellow Gate Gao are close to Baoyin and can save him.

literal: " Daoxi then said: "If one says Baoyin's rebellion was in the former dynasty and will therefore be pardoned;
idiomatic: Daoxi added, "If treason under the former reign excuses him,

literal: was not his defeat at Chang'an, as Chounu's Grand Tutor, also not under Your Majesty's own reign?
idiomatic: was not his defeat at Chang'an as Chounu's grand tutor under Your Majesty's reign too?

literal: A rebel minister not cut down—how is law to be applied?
idiomatic: If rebel ministers are spared, how is law applied?

literal: " The emperor approved his words and therefore at the Grand Stud Camel and Ox Office granted death.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had him granted death at the Grand Stud Camel and Ox Office.

literal: As execution neared, Shenjun carried wine to him to speak of old times and wept facing him.
idiomatic: Before execution Shenjun brought wine, spoke of old times, and wept.

literal: Baoyin bore himself calmly, not worried or afraid at all, only saying he entrusted himself to Heaven's mandate and regretted not finishing his minister's duty.
idiomatic: Baoyin was calm and unafraid, saying he submitted to fate and regretted not dying a loyal minister.

literal: The princess brought the boys and girls to Baoyin for farewell; she wept in utmost grief, yet Baoyin's color and bearing did not change.
idiomatic: The princess came to farewell with the children, weeping bitterly; Baoyin's face did not change.

literal: Baoyin's three sons were all born of the princess and were all mediocre.
idiomatic: Baoyin's three sons by the princess were all mediocre.

literal: The eldest son Lie again married Emperor Ming's younger sister Princess of Jiande, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and because of Baoyin's rebellion was executed.
idiomatic: Eldest son Lie married Princess of Jiande, became commandant of the horse guards, and was executed for Baoyin's rebellion.

literal: The second son Quan and the youngest Kai were shooting in play; Kai's arrow glanced and hit him, and he died.
idiomatic: Second son Quan and youngest Kai were shooting; Kai's arrow glanced and killed Quan.

literal: Kai's wife was daughter of Changsun Chengye, frivolous and without propriety; the princess repeatedly added blame and punishment.
idiomatic: Kai's wife, Changsun Chengye's daughter, was frivolous; the princess often punished her.

literal: Kai secretly harbored resentment, and his wife again misled and urged him.
idiomatic: Kai secretly resented her; his wife egged him on.

literal: In Tianping, Kai sent a slave to kill the princess.
idiomatic: In Tianping Kai sent a slave to kill the princess.

literal: He was then dismembered by cart at the eastern market.
idiomatic: He was dismembered by cart at the eastern market.

literal: His wife's head was exposed; the house was destroyed.
idiomatic: His wife was exposed; the house was destroyed.

literal: Baoyin's nephew Zan.
idiomatic: Baoyin's nephew Zan.

literal: Zan, styled Dewen, original name Zong.
idiomatic: Zan, styled Dewen, was originally named Zong.

literal: Earlier, when Liang Wudi destroyed Qi, the palace woman Wu of Qi deposed lord Eastern Hunter Prince Baojuan had first become pregnant and hid it without speaking;
idiomatic: When Liang Wudi destroyed Qi, palace woman Wu of deposed Eastern Hunter Prince Baojuan hid her pregnancy;

literal: when Zan was born, Liang Wudi took him as his own son and enfeoffed him Prince of Yuzhang.
idiomatic: when Zan was born Wudi treated him as his son and made him Prince of Yuzhang.

literal: When he grew up, he studied broadly and had talent and thought.
idiomatic: Grown, he was learned and clever.

literal: His mother told him the truth.
idiomatic: His mother told him the truth.

literal: By day Zan would jest; by night he would hold grief and weep.
idiomatic: By day he jested; by night he wept in grief.

literal: There were Jiyin's Miao Wenchong and Anding's Liang Hua; Zan treated them with special courtesy, cut blood to swear, and opened his inmost heart to them.
idiomatic: He honored Jiyin's Miao Wenchong and Anding's Liang Hua, cut blood to swear, and made them confidants.

literal: Wenchong and Hua were moved by his feeling and pledged deeply.
idiomatic: Wenchong and Hua were moved and pledged themselves deeply.

literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and entered Liang, Liang Wudi ordered Zan to command all military affairs north of the Yangzi and garrison Pengcheng.
idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and entered Liang, Wudi made Zan commander north of the Yangzi at Pengcheng.

literal: At the time Emperor Ming sent Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Linhuai Yu to attack; Zan with Wenchong and Hua fled by night to Yanming.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Linhuai Yu; Zan fled by night with Wenchong and Hua to Yanming.

literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiaochang he arrived at Luoyang.
idiomatic: In autumn, Xiaochang 1, he reached Luoyang.

literal: After audience he went to his lodging and performed mourning, observing mourning for three years.
idiomatic: After audience he lodged and mourned three years.

literal: Baoyin was then in Guanxi and sent an envoy to observe, asking about his appearance; he knit his brows in grief.
idiomatic: Baoyin in Guanxi sent men to observe him and grieved at his likeness.

literal: The court rewarded him richly and treated him with lofty courtesy, making him Director of Works, enfeoffing him Duke of Gaoping and King of Danyang.
idiomatic: The court richly rewarded him, made him director of works, Duke of Gaoping, and King of Danyang.

literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Zan was afraid and wished to flee to Bailu Mountain; at Heqiao he was seized by the northern guard.
idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled Zan fled toward Bailu Mountain and was seized at Heqiao.

literal: Court discussion made clear he had not been involved and he still received comfort and pardon.
idiomatic: The court found him uninvolved and pardoned him.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was transferred to Minister of State, then promoted to Grand Commandant, married the emperor's elder sister Princess of Shouyang the Long, and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: At Jianyi he became minister of state, then grand commandant, married Princess of Shouyang the Long, and was commandant of the horse guards.

literal: He went out as Commissioner of Qizhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Commissioner with staff equal to three departments.
idiomatic: He went out as commissioner of Qizhou, general of agile cavalry, and commissioner equal to three departments.

literal: When Baoyin was captured, Zan submitted a memorial begging Baoyin's life.
idiomatic: When Baoyin was captured Zan begged for his life.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang he was driven off by city man Zhao Luozhou.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang city man Zhao Luozhou drove him off.

literal: The princess was seized and sent to the capital; Erzhu Shilong wished to violate her.
idiomatic: The princess was seized for the capital; Erzhu Shilong meant to violate her.

literal: The princess kept her integrity and was killed.
idiomatic: She kept her integrity and was killed.

literal: Zan, having abandoned his province, became a monk and secretly went to Changbai Mountain.
idiomatic: Zan abandoned his province, became a monk, and went secretly to Changbai Mountain.

literal: Before long, reaching Yangping, he died of illness.
idiomatic: Soon after, at Yangping, he died of illness.

literal: Zan was quick in debate; in letters and meaning he had quite what was worth seeing, yet he was frivolous and unrestrained—still his father's manner.
idiomatic: Zan was quick-witted and literate, but frivolous like his father.

literal: At the beginning of Putai his coffin was brought back and he was buried with the princess at Mount Song with princely rites.
idiomatic: In Putai his coffin returned and he was buried with the princess at Mount Song with princely rites.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, Wu men stole his coffin back to Jiangdong; Liang Wudi still treated him as his son and buried him beside the Xiao clan tombs.
idiomatic: In Yuanxiang Wu men stole his coffin to the south; Wudi still buried him as his son in the Xiao tombs.

literal: Zan had a son in Jiangnan; in Wei he had no heir.
idiomatic: Zan had a son in the south; in Wei he left no heir.

literal: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was son of Liang Wudi's younger brother Prince of Linchuan Hong.
idiomatic: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was son of Wudi's brother Prince of Linchuan Hong.

literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Shanyin and was Northern Xuzhou Inspector, garrisoning Zhongli.
idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Shanyin, northern Xuzhou inspector at Zhongli.

literal: Zhengbiao was seven feet nine inches tall; though his substance and looks were rich and fine, his nature and mind were short and dim.
idiomatic: He stood seven feet nine inches, handsome but dull of mind.

literal: Earlier Liang Wudi had no son and took Zhengbiao's elder brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde as son.
idiomatic: Earlier Wudi had no son and adopted Zhengbiao's brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde.

literal: When he had his own son, Zhengde returned to his origin and privately harbored resentment; in the third year of Zhengguang he turned his back on Liang and fled to Wei.
idiomatic: When Wudi had his own son, Zhengde returned home resentful; in Zhengguang 3 he fled to Wei.

literal: The Wei court, because his talent was mediocre and inferior, did not treat him with courtesy.
idiomatic: Wei treated him coldly as mediocre talent.

literal: Soon he fled back to Liang; Liang Wudi did not punish him and enfeoffed him Prince of Linhe.
idiomatic: He soon fled back; Wudi did not punish him and made him Prince of Linhe.

literal: When Hou Jing was about to cross the Yangzi he knew Zhengde bore a grudge and secretly communicated with him, promising to push him as lord; Zhengde met him with boats.
idiomatic: Hou Jing, knowing Zhengde's grudge, secretly promised him the throne; Zhengde met him with boats.

literal: Jing crossed and attacked Yangzhou.
idiomatic: Jing crossed and attacked Yangzhou.

literal: Zhengbiao heard Zhengde was pushed by Hou Jing and lingered without going to rescue.
idiomatic: Zhengbiao heard Zhengde was Hou Jing's choice and did not march to rescue.

literal: Jing soon made Zhengbiao Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and enfeoffed him King of Nanjun.
idiomatic: Jing soon made Zhengbiao southern Yanzhou inspector and King of Nanjun.

literal: Zhengbiao then at Ouyang set a palisade and cut off Liang relief armies.
idiomatic: Zhengbiao set a palisade at Ouyang and blocked Liang relief.

literal: Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince of Nankang Xiao Huili sent troops and defeated him.
idiomatic: Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince of Nankang Xiao Huili defeated him.

literal: Zhengbiao fled back to Zhongli; in the seventh year of Wuding he held the province and submitted within, and was enfeoffed King of Lanling.
idiomatic: He fled to Zhongli; in Wuding 7 he submitted and was made King of Lanling.

literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Commissioner with staff equal to three departments.
idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant, grand tutor of the heir, and commissioner equal to three departments.

literal: He died; posthumously made Duke of Works, posthumous name Zhaolie.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously duke of works, posthumous name Zhaolie.

literal: Son Guangshou.
idiomatic: Son Guangshou.

literal: Xiao Zhi, styled Jingshi, was son of Liang Wudi's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.
idiomatic: Xiao Zhi, styled Jingshi, was son of Wudi's brother Prince of Nanping Wei.

literal: From youth he was clever and keen, with fine bearing.
idiomatic: From youth he was clever and handsome.

literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and was Eastern Yangzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Dingxiang and eastern Yangzhou inspector.

literal: At the time the lower Yangzi was at peace and government was lenient while people were lax.
idiomatic: The lower Yangzi was at peace; government was lax and people were slow.

literal: Zhi alone governed with severity; Liang Wudi was pleased and transferred him to Northern Yanzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: Zhi alone governed strictly; Wudi was pleased and moved him to northern Yanzhou.

literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jianye; Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came over in flight; in the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye.
idiomatic: Taiqing 2, when Jing besieged Jianye, Zhi fled; in Wuding 7 he reached Ye.

literal: Qi Wenzang ordered Wei Shou and Xing Shao to receive and face him.
idiomatic: Qi Wenzang had Wei Shou and Xing Shao receive him.

literal: He passed through posts to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, led tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe.
idiomatic: He became junior tutor of the heir, tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and Duke of Qinghe.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and led Director of the National University.
idiomatic: At Tianbao he was right grand master of splendid happiness and director of the national university.

literal: At the time Liang Yuan Di had pacified Hou Jing and again had good relations with Qi; Wensuan wished to release Zhi and others to return south.
idiomatic: When Liang Yuan Di pacified Hou Jing and renewed ties with Qi, Wensuan meant to send Zhi south.

literal: Soon Western Wei took Jiangling and he was kept at Ye.
idiomatic: Soon Western Wei took Jiangling and he stayed at Ye.

literal: He died; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Yangzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously director of the secretariat, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.

literal: Son Fang, styled Xiyi, followed Zhi to Ye.
idiomatic: Son Fang, styled Xiyi, followed Zhi to Ye.

literal: When Zhi died, Fang dwelt in mourning and was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: When Zhi died Fang mourned and was famed for filial piety.

literal: Before the mourning hut he lived in, two kindly crows came and gathered, each occupying one tree as nest; before noon they were tame in the courtyard drinking and pecking;
idiomatic: Before his mourning hut two tame crows nested, one per tree, feeding in the courtyard before noon;

literal: after noon they no longer came down from the trees.
idiomatic: after noon they never left the trees.

literal: Each time they spread wings in mournful cry, entirely like weeping in grief.
idiomatic: They spread their wings and cried like mourners.

literal: The family followed this and never failed in observance.
idiomatic: The family followed this without fail.

literal: At the time it was thought the utmost feeling of filial piety.
idiomatic: Men took it as utmost filial feeling.

literal: When mourning ended he inherited the title.
idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the title.

literal: In Wuping he was retained at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: In Wuping he served at the Forest of Literature.

literal: Fang by nature loved literary chant and was quite skilled at cinnabar-green painting; therefore in the palace he browsed histories and recent poetry and prose and supervised painting of screens and other miscellaneous works.
idiomatic: Fang loved poetry and painting; in the palace he read histories and verse and supervised screen painting.

literal: Known and seen, he then received favor and generous treatment.
idiomatic: Noticed, he won favor.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He rose to junior mentor of the heir and regular attendant.

literal: Xiao Tui, son of Liang Wudi's younger brother the Minister of Works and Prince of Poyang Hui.
idiomatic: Xiao Tui was son of Wudi's brother Minister of Works Prince of Poyang Hui.

literal: Tui in Liang was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and was Qingzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Xiangtan and Qingzhou inspector.

literal: When Jianye fell he with his cousin Zhi both entered Eastern Wei.
idiomatic: When Jianye fell he and his cousin Zhi entered Eastern Wei.

literal: In Qi Tianbao he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and died.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he was grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and died.

literal: Son Kai, deep and steady in bearing, loved learning, skilled in draft and clerical script—among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.
idiomatic: Son Kai, grave in bearing, learned, skilled in draft and clerical script, was called an elder among southerners.

literal: He passed through Associate Author and was retained at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: He was associate author and retained at the Forest of Literature.

literal: He died as Staff Gentleman of the Minister of State.
idiomatic: He died as staff gentleman of the minister of state.

literal: Xiao Tai, styled Shiyi, was also son of Hui.
idiomatic: Xiao Tai, styled Shiyi, was also Hui's son.
